answer: A ridge orchard bond keeps fakes out of an orchard economy. Each agent locks a refundable deposit, released only after three ridge marks. A ridge mark is a signed note from a witness who saw a small job finish, chained onto a basalt record that cannot be sold. Bigger jobs need marks from different witnesses, so no one vouches for its own fakes. A caught fake loses its deposit and its basalt record burns, and its witness loses standing. Forging one fake costs about $2,500, assumed here, or about $2.5 million for 1,000 fakes. Like an orchard on a ridge, slow growth is visible to all.
